the amount of aminoacyl-tRNA in an amino acid starved culture of E. coli is not necessarily correlated with the rate at which the organism is synthesizing RNA.
the level of unchared tRNA is not the only factor that controls the rate of RNA sythesis.
the level of charged aminoacyl-tRNA is the key factor in amino acid control of ribonucleiic acid synthesis.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the mechanism of the regulation of RNA synthesis in bacteria by amino acid limitation.
the regulation of RNA synthesis in E. coli and the role of charged tRNA in this process.
the regulation of RNA synthesis by amino acid starvation in Escherich...
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the amino acid control mechanism is not the same for each amino acid and that the aminoacyl-tRNA plays an important role in this control.
the aminoacyl-tRNA is the regulatory factor in the control of RNA synthesis in E. coli.
the charged tRNA, and not the uncharged, plays the key role in the amino acid regulation of RNA synthesis.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
aminoacylation of the tRNA is a prerequisite to the amino acid control.
amino acids are required for RNA synthesis and that the amino acid controls RNA synthesis by controlling the availability of charged transfer RNA.
the amino acid control system is sensitive to the level of charged tRNA.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the level of charged tRNA is an important factor in controlling RNA synthesis.
the level of charged tRNA is an important determinant of the rate of RNA production in E. coli.
the level of unbound tRNA is not a direct indicator of the amount of protein synthesis in a cell.
